{{nihongo|'''Ogura Shrine'''|巨椋神社|Ogura-jinja}} is a [[Shinto shrine]] located in Ogura-chō, Terauchi, [[Uji]], [[Kyoto Prefecture]]. The shrine is listed in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]] as a small shrine in [[Yamashiro Province]]. According to shrine tradition, it was founded by imperial order of [[Emperor Saga]], though it is more likely that it originated when the ancient Ogura clan enshrined their ancestral deity. The Ogura clan is listed under "Divine descent" in the [[Shinsen Shōjiroku]]. During the late Heian period, it came under the patronage of the [[Fujiwara clan]] and became a Kasuga-line shrine, being called Kasuga Shrine until early modern times.

'''Ogura Shrine'''（おぐらじんじゃ）is a shrine in Terauchi, Ogura-chō, {{ill|Uji|Q326956|qid=Q326956}}, {{ill|Kyoto Prefecture|ace|Prefektur Kyoto|af|Kioto-prefektuur|an|Prefectura de Kyoto|ar|كيوتو (محافظة)|ast|Prefeutura de Kyoto|az|Kioto prefekturası|azb|کیوتو اوستانی|ban|Préféktur Kyoto|bat_smg|Kijuota prefektūra|be|Кіёта (прэфектура)|bg|Киото (префектура)|bn|কিয়োতো প্রশাসনিক অঞ্চল|ca|Prefectura de Kyoto|cdo|Gĭng-dŭ-hū|ce|Киото (префектура)|ceb|Kyōto-fu|ckb|پارێزگای کیۆتۆ|cs|Prefektura Kjóto|cy|Kyoto (talaith)|da|Kyoto-præfekturet|de|Präfektur Kyōto|eo|Gubernio Kioto|es|Prefectura de Kioto|et|Kyōto prefektuur|eu|Kyoto (prefektura)|fa|استان کیوتو|fi|Kioton prefektuuri|fr|Préfecture de Kyoto|frr|Kyōto (Prefektüür)|ga|Maoracht Kyoto|gl|Prefectura de Kyoto|hak|Kîn-tû-fú|he|קיוטו (מחוז)|hr|Kyōto (prefektura)|hu|Kiotó prefektúra|hy|Կիոտո (պրեֆեկտուրա)|id|Prefektur Kyoto|ilo|Prepektura ti Kyoto|is|Kyoto-hérað|it|Prefettura di Kyoto|ja|京都府|ka|კიოტოს პრეფექტურა|km|ក្យូតុ(ខេត្ត)|ko|교토부|la|Kyotensis|lt|Kioto prefektūra|lv|Kioto prefektūra|mk|Кјото (префектура)|mni|ꯀ꯭ꯌꯣꯇꯣ ꯂꯝꯈꯥꯢ|mr|क्योतो प्रांत|ms|Wilayah Kyoto|my|ကျိုတိုစီရင်စု|nl|Kyoto (prefectuur)|no|Kyoto (prefektur)|os|Киото (префектурæ)|pam|Prepektura ning Kyoto|pl|Prefektura Kioto|pnb|ضلع کیوٹو|pt|Quioto (prefeitura)|ro|Prefectura Kyoto|ru|Киото (префектура)|sco|Kyoto Prefectur|sd|ڪيوٽو پريفيڪچر|se|Kyōto prefektuvra|sh|Prefektura Kyōto|si|ක්යෝතෝ ප්‍රාන්තය|simple|Kyoto Prefecture|sk|Kjóto (prefektúra)|sl|Prefektura Kjoto|sr|Префектура Кјото|su|Préféktur Kyoto|sv|Kyoto prefektur|sw|Mkoa wa Kyoto|ta|கியோத்தோ நகரிய மாநிலம்|tg|Префектураи Кёто|th|จังหวัดเกียวโต|tl|Prepektura ng Kyoto|tr|Kyoto (prefektörlük)|tt|Киото (префектура)|uk|Префектура Кіото|ur|کیوتو پریفیکچر|uz|Kioto prefekturasi|vec|Prefetura de Kyoto|vi|Kyōto|war|Kyoto (prefektura)|wuu|京都府|zh|京都府|zh_classical|京都府|zh_min_nan|Kiaⁿ-to͘-hú|zh_yue|京都府|qid=Q120730}}. It is a {{ill|Shikinai Shosha|ja|式内小社|simple|Shikinai Shosha|qid=Q134917287|lt=Shikinai small shrine}}, and its former {{ill|Shakaku|Q10444029|qid=Q10444029}} was {{ill|Son-sha|ja|村社|qid=Q134917284}}.

It is thought to have been the clan shrine of the ancient clan Ogura-no-Muraji, and is said to have begun when they enshrined their ancestral deity<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=edited by Kunihiko Shimonaka |title=Place Names of Kyoto Prefecture |publisher=Heibonsha |year=1981/03/13 |page=108 |isbn=}}</ref>.

== History ==
== Foundation ==
According to shrine tradition, it was founded by imperial order of {{ill|Emperor Saga|Q316654|qid=Q316654}}, but it is more likely that it originated when the ancient clan Ogura-no-Muraji enshrined its ancestral deity. Ogura-no-Muraji is an ancient clan listed under "Divine descent" in the {{ill|Shinsen Shōjiroku|Q1045362|qid=Q1045362}}.

== Outline ==
In the late Heian period it became a place of worship for the {{ill|Fujiwara clan|Q641628|qid=Q641628}}, became a Kasuga-line shrine, and was called Kasuga Shrine until early modern times. There is a precinct shrine, Komori Shrine (Uji). It originally stood at Kasuga-no-mori in Ogura-chō, and was later moved to its current location<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=edited by Tatsusaburō Hayashiya and Kenzirō Fujioka |title=History of Uji City 1: Ancient History and Landscape |publisher=Uji City Office |year=1974/07/01 |page=283 |isbn=}}</ref>.

== Precincts ==
In the precincts are giant hackberry and zelkova trees said to be at least 700-800 years old<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=edited by Tatsusaburō Hayashiya and Kenzirō Fujioka |title=History of Uji City 6: Life and Environment in Western Uji River Area |publisher=Uji City Office |year=1981/03/01 |page=514 |isbn=}}</ref>.

== Komori Shrine ==
[[ファイル:Ogura Jinja Uji Keidaisha Komori Jinja.jpg|thumb|150px|{{center|Komori Shrine honden}}]]
=== Enshrined deities ===
Hiruko-no-Kami（ひるこのかみ）

Ame-no-Iwakusubune-no-Kami（あめのいわくすぶねのかみ）

=== History ===
It is said that Prince Koretaka, after defeating three giant kites that attacked children, built a shrine in Ogura on his way back from Kawachi. Since then, it came to be revered as a protector of children, thus "Komori Shrine." Today, the main shrine Ogura Shrine is often mistaken for Komori Shrine, but Komori Shrine exists separately as a precinct shrine within Ogura Shrine<ref>{{Cite book|和書|author=edited by Tatsusaburō Hayashiya and Kenzirō Fujioka |title=History of Uji City 1: Ancient History and Landscape |publisher=Uji City Office |year=1974/07/01 |page=284 |isbn=}}</ref>.

== Monument of Gyokuro Tea Origin ==
Within the precincts is a "Monument of the Origin of Gyokuro Tea Production," based on an anecdote about the birth of {{ill|Gyokuro|Q1424874|qid=Q1424874}} by Yamamoto Kahei<ref>{{Cite web|和書|url=https://www.pref.kyoto.jp/nosan/documents/1312184290019.pdf|title=Tour of the Kyoto-Yamashiro Uji tea region|publisher=Kyoto Prefecture|accessdate=2022-06-13}}</ref>.
